elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term"), and the conditional automatic-renewal elements are not all satisfied — the opt-out window is 60 days (not ≤30) and no Vendor renewal reminder is added — so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: The renewal term is defined by reference — "an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — and no Service Option Attachment term length is in the cited text or resolved definitions, so a term exceeding 12 months (automatic multi-year renewal) cannot be excluded on this record.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires notice "at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred opt-out ceiling. To meet preferred, change the operative figure to 30 days for Customer's non-renewal notice.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered language; the margin comment only mentions the 60-day reminder as our preferred position, and a promise in a comment is not operative. A sentence obliging Vendor to notify Customer at least 60 days before each renewal date would be required.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: the renewal clause carries the Service Option Attachment forward on the same terms for a like-duration term and contains no uplift or repricing mechanic, so no renewal price-increase cap is required by this element.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered operative text: "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term" — the window is exactly 60 days, at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a token-matching artifact (the original spelled-out "ninety (90)" form was replaced with the bare numeral "60"); on substantive inspection the ≤60-day requirement is satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: the renewal provision provides only for automatic continuation for a like-duration term and grants no renewal uplift right. The separate §13.1 unilateral price-change mechanic is a change-of-terms right (post-12-month, 90 days' notice, fee-free exit), not a renewal repricing term, and is correctly not double-flagged here.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single operative edit brings the non-renewal notice window to 60 days, and the renewal clause permits no price uplift so the 5% cap element is not engaged. The classification as a deviation with a redline is correct because the original 90-day window failed the fallback ceiling.

Preferred level is not complete: the opt-out remains at 60 rather than 30 days, and no Vendor 60-day renewal reminder obligation was inserted in operative text (it is only referenced in the margin comment).

Renewal term length is left as "equal in duration to the previous term." If any Service Option Attachment runs longer than 12 months this is an automatic multi-year renewal and touches walk-away territory; the drafter should confirm attachment durations and, if any exceed 12 months, fix the renewal term at 12 months in the operative clause.

Minimality is satisfied: only the numeral in the notice window was altered; the mutual ("either party") notice right, the per-Attachment structure, the writing requirement and the term-end anchor are all retained, and no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were added.

Intent is preserved: the clause still operates per Service Option Attachment, the termination-by-notice mechanic and its end-of-term anchor are unchanged, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling. Minor drafting nit only: the document style uses spelled-out numerals with digits in parentheses ("ninety (90)"), so "sixty (60)" would match house style — stylistic, not a minimality or intent defect.
Deterministic evidence note: the "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" check failed on pattern matching, not substance; the rendered clause plainly states 60 days.
